analysis: Examined the head text of docs/developer/test.md (lines 3187-3658, which only describe test suites and add no behavior) and the patch to scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py. The test.md changes (visible in the file_changes patch excerpt) are a date bump and a paragraph describing run-isolation regression tests. No security control, key handling, attestation, cache, or encryption behavior changes in either file. The Python change adds a run_labels helper and tests asserting that the router sends an X-Darkbloom-Run-Scoped-Labels header and accepts only labels qualified with the current run id (-run-<id>). Generic, other-run, or appended-label grants fall back to Blacksmith. Two runs must not select each other's registered runner. The change is test-only and tightens CI runner isolation. It does not touch the provider/coordinator trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-011) or the listed assets, and the retained T-041 definition concerns the provider's prefix-cache storage, which is unrelated. The real enforcement lives in .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml and the external routing plane, neither of which is in this batch. The tests only model GitHub's all-label matching and are not evidence about the actual workflow or live runners. Open question for integration: confirm the workflow script actually sends the header and validates run-qualified labels the way these tests assert. I identified no regression from the supplied evidence.
